neighbours.label: carbon credits and offsets as a traded instrument
fire: Airlines may purchase carbon offsets to cover the emissions of each flight.
The forest project earns credits that are traded on the voluntary market.
Polluters that exceed their cap can buy carbon credits from cleaner firms.
The company offsets its remaining emissions by funding verified tree planting schemes.
Each carbon credit represents one tonne of avoided greenhouse gas.
Brokers sell offset credits from wind farms to European buyers.
The registry certifies the emission reductions and issues tradable carbon credits.
Critics doubt that buying forest offsets really cancels a firm's emissions.
quiet: Airlines may fit lighter seats to lower the emissions of each flight.
The forest project protects birds that nest on the steep slopes.
Polluters that exceed their cap can be fined by the regulators.
The company cut its remaining emissions by replacing its old boilers.
Each kilogram of coal releases a large amount of greenhouse gas.
Engineers install turbines from wind farms for European utilities.
The agency measures the emission levels and publishes yearly climate reports.
Critics doubt that replacing old boilers really lowers a firm's emissions.
